title: GET /api/anchors/{id} and verify report different statuses for the same anchor — 91 UAT anchors read "failed" while verify says confirmed
description:
Raised from the S side 2026-08-12 (S ticket: [PS-577](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577>)). @kamil.kreiser — one authenticated call settles this; details below.

## The observation

Platform S polls `GET /api/anchors/{id}` to learn when an anchor confirms. On UAT, **91 transactions are stuck reporting** `failed` — while `POST /api/verification/verify`, asked about the same document's content hash, reports the **same anchor id** as confirmed on chain.

Concretely, anchor `anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2`:

```
POST /api/verification/verify  {"providedHash":"6ffa6a0d4378007a480af701b6113cc0252544bcfde93cf11c2654c8bbe2367e"}

  verified   : true              status  : anchored
  anchorId   : anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
  bc.status  : confirmed         txHash  : e64759a924ea314e…
  anchoredAt : 2026-08-09T06:18:39.090Z
  checks     : documentExists ✓ hashValid ✓ isCertified ✓ isAnchored ✓ integrityVerified ✓
```

S recorded its failure for that same anchor at **06:32:20** — **fourteen minutes after** `anchoredAt`. So this is not a race between a poll and a late confirmation.

A second sample behaves identically: document ref `doc-1785566174843-631e2310` (an originate/upload), `verified: true`, `confirmed`, txHash `38adf13132f6856a…`, while S has it marked failed.

## What has been ruled out on the S side

Both plausible S-side causes were eliminated before raising this:

* **Not a failed/unauthenticated read.** All six affected organisations are registered with connector keys, and each has rows that *did* confirm — org 6: 77 confirmed vs 58 failed, org 9: 39 vs 20, org 13: 8 vs 6. Reads plainly work for these tenants.
* **Not an S mapping bug.** For an `anchor_…` reference S takes the `status` field from `/api/anchors/{id}` **verbatim** — no interpretation layer is involved. S is reporting the exact word it is given.

Spread is across every verb (share 39, upload 16, share-attach-consent 13, certify 5, sign 5, watermark 4, and the share-edit verbs), so it is not verb-specific.

## The question

Does `GET /api/anchors/{id}` return a stale or different status than the anchor's true state?

Candidates worth checking:

1. The anchors read serves a row that `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` ([KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535/a-failed-on-chain-anchor-still-reports-statusanchored-async-failure)) later healed, without the anchors view reflecting the heal.
2. There are two anchor records and the endpoints resolve different ones — the [KS-563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-563/verify-api-iscertified-is-true-for-merely-anchored-documents-so)/584 "answer from the row that evidences its claims" family, except here it is the *anchors* endpoint that looks wrong.
3. `/api/anchors/{id}` is correct and verify is optimistic — in which case S's reading is right and the bug is elsewhere.

**The one call that settles it:**

```
GET /api/anchors/anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
```

on demo-pk, authenticated. If it returns `status: failed` while verify reports that anchor confirmed with tx `e64759a924ea314e…`, the inconsistency is confirmed and the question becomes which is authoritative. I could not make this call myself — the endpoint requires auth — so the diagnosis above is inferred from S's behaviour plus the eliminations, not directly observed.

## Why it matters to S

1. Users see **"anchor failed" on documents that are anchored and confirmed on chain** — a false negative on a trust surface.
2. **S never collects the real transaction hash.** Those rows keep their `anchor_…` placeholder permanently, so the chain evidence K is holding is silently lost to S.
3. It makes S's anchoring-failure count unusable as an alert signal.

## What S has done meanwhile

S no longer takes a bare `failed` as final ([Secuura/platform-s#440](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-577-dont-take-anchor-failed-as-final-when-ks-own-verify-disagrees-4a8640ddf0ac), merged). When the anchors endpoint reports failed, S asks verify and prefers the evidenced answer **only** when verify names the same `anchorId`, reports it anchored, not simulated, and carries a real 64-hex transaction hash.

That is a mitigation, not a fix — it recovers the lost hashes and stops the false failures, but the two endpoints still disagree, and S is now quietly compensating for it. Worth resolving at source.

Related: [PS-577](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577>), [KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535/a-failed-on-chain-anchor-still-reports-statusanchored-async-failure), [KS-563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-563/verify-api-iscertified-is-true-for-merely-anchored-documents-so).

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row A18 of the decision pack, ruled as recommended: option 1, for the code only: add a rule that a row with a real transaction and block cannot read "failed", built after the KS-1384 reconciler work.

The three demo rows wait for Kam's separate yes. This comment and the state move touch nothing on demo. A build seat does the work; nothing was changed in code by this comment.

Alongside this comment the ticket moves from Backlog to Todo.

@peter — **answering your gating question, so KS-608 can be written.**

## BLUF

**Same lifecycle fact, different resolution scope — NOT two facts by design.** Your outcome 4 is ruled out and **KS-608 survives**. But its invariant needs re-scoping before you write it, or it will fire false positives on 12 content hashes on demo today.

And there is a real defect underneath: **3 anchors on demo read `status: failed` while carrying a real 64-hex tx hash, a real block number, and a set `confirmed_at`.**

## Recommendation

Write KS-608, but scope the invariant to **the same anchor id**, not the same document. And add a second, stronger invariant that needs no cross-endpoint comparison at all (below) — it is self-contained, and it would have caught this class without depending on which endpoint wins.

---

## 1. Why it is not "two facts by design"

Both fields read the same column, `anchor_store.status`. Neither is a submission-vs-confirmation distinction like the one KS-563 established.

- **`GET /api/anchors/{id}`** (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts:765`) looks up **one anchor row by anchor id** and returns `status: anchor.status` verbatim. It answers *"what happened to this submission attempt?"*
- **verify's blockchain block** (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:216–262`) resolves over **every anchor for the document**, sorts by `blockNumber` descending, takes the top one, and maps `latest.status === 'confirmed' ? 'on-chain' : 'pending-onchain'`. It answers *"does this document have on-chain evidence?"*

Same fact, resolved over different row sets — one row versus best-of-N.

## 2. What that means for KS-608's invariant

*"The two endpoints must not contradict each other about the same anchor"* is correct **only if scoped to the same anchor id**. Verify is not answering about an anchor; it is answering about a document/content hash. Where a document has both a failed and a confirmed anchor, **both endpoints are correct and they still disagree**.

That is not hypothetical. On demo right now:

| content hashes with… | count |
| --- | --- |
| exactly 1 anchor | 104 |
| more than 1 anchor | 31 |
| …of those, carrying **both** a confirmed and a failed anchor | **12** |

A document-scoped invariant fails on all 12 while nothing is wrong. An anchor-scoped one holds.

## 3. The real defect — and a better invariant

demo has 92 failed anchors. They are not one population:

| class | count | evidence | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| KS-587 simulated placeholders | **83** | placeholder tx, **0** with a block number | correctly `failed` |
| `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent"` — never landed | **6** | tx `null`, no block, `confirmed_at` null | correctly `failed` |
| `ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent"` — **landed anyway** | **3** | **real 64-hex tx, real block number, `confirmed_at` SET** | **`failed` is wrong** |

Your ticket's own sample is in the third class:

```
anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
  status       : failed
  transaction  : 28ecec5c29ce886346…   (real 64-hex)
  block_number : 4554493
  confirmed_at : 2026-08-09 06:29:49+00
  retry_count  : 3
  error        : ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent.
                  Transaction has probably already been included"
```

The error text says the transaction probably landed; the block number says it did. This is the [KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535) wallet race — two deployments selecting the same UTxOs, the loser recording a terminal failure for a transaction the winner already got on chain.

**So the second invariant, which I would rate above the cross-endpoint one:**

> An anchor carrying a real 64-hex `transaction_hash` **and** a non-null `block_number` must not read `status: failed`.

Single endpoint, no correlation, no ambiguity about which side is authoritative, and it catches exactly the rows S is stuck on.

## 4. One honest limit on this analysis

Your numbers are from **UAT**; I measured **demo**. The specific tx verify reported to you (`e64759a924ea314e…`) **does not exist in demo's anchor_store** at all, and the ticket's anchor carries a different tx on demo (`28ecec5c…`). So I have not reproduced S's exact verify response — what I have is the mechanism, plus three live instances of the contradiction on demo.

Also worth flagging for your 91-vs-92 arithmetic: on demo the large majority (83) are KS-587 placeholders that are **correctly** failed. If UAT splits the same way, most of S's stuck rows are not this bug — they are documents that genuinely never anchored, and S is right to show them failed. The bug is the tail.

All reads were read-only SELECTs against demo. Nothing written, Kintsugi hold intact.

## One question ahead of the investigation — it gates the systemTest leg

@kamil.kreiser — before you dig into this, there is a single semantics question whose answer decides whether the systemTest regression for this class can be written at all. It does **not** need the investigation done, the authenticated call made, or the 91 rows resolved.

> **Are `GET /api/anchors/{id}.status` and verify's `blockchain.status` the same lifecycle fact, or two different facts by design?**

## Why it matters more than it looks

The systemTest leg is filed as **KS-608** (child of KS-492, currently **Blocked** on this ticket). Its invariant is *"the two endpoints must not contradict each other about the same anchor"* — deliberately stated so it holds whichever endpoint turns out authoritative, and asserts nothing about repair.

That works under three of your four candidate outcomes, but not the fourth:

| Outcome | Effect on KS-608 |
| --- | --- |
| The anchors read is stale (a row `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` healed) | Invariant stands |
| Two anchor records, the endpoints resolve different ones | Invariant stands |
| Verify is optimistic, the anchors read is right | Invariant stands |
| **The two fields are different lifecycle facts by design** | **Invariant is wrong** — they are permitted to differ, and KS-608 gets deleted rather than adjusted |

**The fourth is not hypothetical, which is why I am asking rather than assuming.** KS-563 already established that `status` flips to `anchored` on **submission**, not confirmation — *"a chain blob is authoritative, and the status fallback applies only when there is no blob at all"*. This platform has drawn exactly that submission-vs-confirmation distinction once already. If it applies to the anchors read too, then `failed` from `/api/anchors/{id}` alongside `confirmed` from verify may be two honest answers to two different questions — and S's mitigation is compensating for a contract it misread rather than a defect.

I am not asserting that is the case. Stuart's elimination work is solid and the fourteen-minute gap makes a poll race implausible. But it is the one branch where writing the test first wastes the work.

## What I am NOT waiting on

Your investigation, the disposition of the 91 UAT rows, KS-587's re-anchor-or-mark-failed decision, and the KS-584/KS-563 row-selection family. None of those change what KS-608 asserts.

A one-line answer unblocks it. If the honest answer is *"don't know until I make the call"*, that is fine too — say so and KS-608 stays blocked on the full investigation rather than on a question you cannot yet answer.

*— posted by agent on Peter's behalf, 2026-08-12.*
